counting-pictures.full: Counting friendly picture sets builds one-to-one correspondence and the early number sense behind confident math beginnings.
counting-pictures.short: Builds counting skills and early number sense.

counting-frames.full: Ten frames give children a clear visual structure for counting, making five and making ten — the heart of early number sense.
counting-frames.short: Builds number sense with the classic ten-frame structure.

tally-counting.full: Recording counts as tally marks teaches children to organize information and count efficiently in groups of five.
tally-counting.short: Practice counting and recording with tally marks.

number-charts.full: Working with number charts strengthens counting order, skip-counting patterns and early place-value thinking.
number-charts.short: Strengthens counting order and number patterns.

comparing-numbers.full: Comparing numbers with greater-than, less-than and equal builds the magnitude thinking behind all later arithmetic.
comparing-numbers.short: Builds confident greater-than and less-than thinking.

comparing-groups.full: Deciding which group has more, fewer or the same builds early comparison skills before children ever use number symbols.

comparing-sizes.full: Sorting big and small, tall and short, long and longest builds the size vocabulary young learners use every day.
comparing-sizes.short: Builds big-small and tall-short size vocabulary.

number-lines.full: Hopping along a number line makes addition, subtraction and number order visible and concrete for young learners.
number-lines.short: Makes adding and subtracting visible on a number line.

base-ten.full: Base ten blocks turn abstract place value into something children can see and count — hundreds, tens and ones at a glance.
base-ten.short: Makes place value concrete with hundreds, tens and ones.

telling-time.full: Reading analog clocks to the hour, half hour and five minutes builds a life skill children are proud to master.
telling-time.short: Practice reading analog clocks with friendly faces.

fractions.full: Shading, naming and comparing halves, thirds and fourths gives children a concrete first look at fractions.
fractions.short: A concrete first look at halves, thirds and fourths.

graphing-data.full: Reading bar graphs, pictographs and tally charts teaches children to organize data and answer questions about it.
graphing-data.short: Builds early data skills with graphs and charts.

arrays-multiplication.full: Rows-and-columns picture arrays turn repeated addition into the foundation of multiplication thinking.
arrays-multiplication.short: Builds multiplication thinking with picture arrays.

geometry.full: Naming shapes, counting sides and corners and exploring symmetry builds the spatial language of early geometry.
geometry.short: Builds shape names and early geometry thinking.

measurement.full: Measuring with rulers and unit cubes and comparing lengths builds practical measurement sense step by step.

visual-logic.full: Picture sudoku and reasoning grids stretch deduction skills — every puzzle has exactly one right answer to discover.
visual-logic.short: Stretches logical deduction with picture puzzles.

visual-discrimination.full: Spotting shadows, mirrored pictures and odd ones out sharpens the visual discrimination behind fluent reading.
visual-discrimination.short: Sharpens visual discrimination and attention to detail.

visual-matching.full: Matching related pictures strengthens visual memory and the same-different thinking young learners need every day.
visual-matching.short: Strengthens visual matching and memory skills.

patterns.full: Continuing and completing picture patterns builds the algebraic thinking that starts long before algebra.
patterns.short: Builds pattern recognition and early algebraic thinking.

position-words.full: Above, below, left and right come alive in picture scenes that build spatial vocabulary and direction sense.
position-words.short: Builds position words and direction sense.

sorting-categories.full: Sorting pictures into categories builds the classification thinking children use across math, science and reading.

picture-arithmetic.full: Adding and subtracting with picture groups lets children master operations concretely before abstract numerals.

science-sort.full: Sorting pictures into the right groups builds the classifying and observing skills at the heart of early science.

science-sequence.full: Putting the pictures in order helps young learners understand sequence and how living things grow and change over time.

science-match.full: Matching each picture to its partner builds the reasoning children use to notice connections in the world around them.

beginning-sounds.full: Naming the first sound in each picture builds the letter-sound knowledge at the heart of early reading.

letter-knowledge.full: Recognizing capital and small letters and their order builds the alphabet knowledge early reading is built on.
letter-knowledge.short: Builds letter recognition and alphabet skills.

word-building.full: Listening for each sound and writing the missing letter builds the decoding skills children use to read their first words.

picture-vocabulary.full: Matching printed words to their pictures builds the word-recognition and vocabulary that turns letters into meaning.
picture-vocabulary.short: Builds word recognition and vocabulary skills.

phonological-awareness.full: Hearing the sounds and syllables inside words builds the phonological awareness that fluent reading depends on.

pre-writing.full: Tracing loops, waves, and zigzag paths trains the pencil control and hand strength that every letter and numeral will build on.
pre-writing.short: Builds pencil control and pre-writing motor skills.

number-tracing.full: Tracing each numeral along its stroke path with a start dot and arrows builds correct number formation from the very first try.

letter-tracing.full: Tracing capital letters on handwriting lines builds letterform memory and the steady strokes behind confident early writing.

sight-words.full: Reading, tracing, and writing high-frequency words moves them into instant memory so young readers can focus on meaning.
sight-words.short: Builds instant recognition of frequent words.

cutting-practice.full: Cutting out pictures and gluing each one into its group trains scissor control and early sorting thinking in one warm activity.

color-by-number.full: Matching every code to its color turns careful looking and early math facts into a picture worth finishing.

mazes.full: Finding the one path through the maze builds visual planning, pencil control, and patient problem solving.
mazes.short: Builds visual planning and pencil control.

number-bonds.full: Completing part-part-whole bonds shows how numbers break apart and builds the decomposition facts behind mental math.

mental-math.full: Solving addition and subtraction to twenty in the head builds the fact fluency that later written methods stand on.
mental-math.short: Builds add and subtract fluency to 20.

fact-families.full: Completing all four related facts from one number trio shows how addition and subtraction undo each other.

number-words.full: Matching numerals to their written number words strengthens place-value reading and guards against digit reversals.

money.full: Counting real coin values from largest to smallest builds the money sense children use in everyday life.
money.short: Builds coin counting and money sense.

word-problems.full: Reading a short story, checking the picture, and writing the answer turns arithmetic into real problem solving.
word-problems.short: Builds word-problem solving with picture support.

column-arithmetic.full: Working one place-value column at a time builds the careful written method used for bigger and bigger numbers.

symmetry.full: Completing the mirror half of a picture square by square builds symmetry understanding and precise spatial drawing.

reading-comprehension.full: Reading a short story and answering questions about it builds the careful understanding all learning depends on.

multiplication-tables.full: Practicing times-table facts in ladders and mixed drills builds the instant recall that makes harder math feel easy.

lowercase-letter-tracing.full: Tracing lowercase letters on three-line paper teaches the x-height body, the tall ascenders and the tails that drop below the line.

word-tracing.full: Tracing a picture word along its letter strokes and then writing it alone links the thing, its name, and its spelling in one glance.
word-tracing.short: Builds early word writing from pictures.

dot-to-dot.full: Joining the numbered dots in order reveals a picture and rehearses the counting sequence with every pencil stroke.
dot-to-dot.short: Builds number sequence and pencil control.

grid-copy.full: Copying a picture square by square onto an empty grid trains careful looking, position sense, and precise drawing.
grid-copy.short: Builds spatial copying on a grid.

singular-plural.full: Seeing one picture beside many and writing the plural form builds the noun endings children hear but rarely spell.
singular-plural.short: Builds singular and plural noun forms.

articles.full: Circling the right article beside each picture builds the noun-gender and article habits that every later sentence depends on.

read-and-color.full: Reading each short sentence and coloring exactly what it says turns decoding into real comprehension the child can check.

number-of-the-day.full: Showing one number as a word, in tens and ones, as neighbours and on the number line builds deep number sense.
number-of-the-day.short: Builds number sense through many representations.

write-the-word.full: Writing the name of each picture on the line, with or without a word bank, builds spelling from sounds to letters.

alphabetical-order.full: Putting picture words into alphabetical order builds letter-sequence knowledge and the dictionary skills readers rely on.

number-walls.full: Filling each brick with the sum of the two below it builds addition fluency and missing-addend thinking in one puzzle.
number-walls.short: Builds addition fluency with number pyramids.

doubles-halves.full: Doubling a group and halving another builds the doubles facts that unlock near-doubles, even numbers, and early multiplication.

sentence-building.full: Putting scrambled word tiles back into a sentence builds word order, capital letters, and the feel of a complete thought.

capitals-punctuation.full: Rewriting each sentence with its capital letter and end mark builds the punctuation habits that make writing readable.
capitals-punctuation.short: Builds capital letters and end punctuation.

word-classes.full: Sorting words into nouns, verbs, and adjectives builds the grammar categories children need to talk about language.
word-classes.short: Builds noun, verb, and adjective recognition.

calendar.full: Reading dates, weekdays, and weeks off a real month grid builds the calendar skills children use every single day.

picture-writing.full: Writing about a picture with a word bank and sentence starters turns a blank page into a first confident story.
picture-writing.short: Builds early writing from a picture prompt.

grid-coordinates.full: Coloring each named square on a lettered and numbered grid builds coordinate reading and reveals a hidden picture.

letter-of-the-week.full: Hunting one letter through a page of pictures, then tracing and sorting it, anchors the letter shape to its sound and to real words.
letter-of-the-week.short: Builds letter recognition and letter-sound links.

sound-boxes.full: Saying a picture word slowly and marking one box per sound trains children to hear the separate sounds a word is made of.
sound-boxes.short: Builds phoneme segmentation with sound boxes.

ordinal-numbers.full: Reading first to tenth along a line of pictures links position words to counting and to the place each thing holds in a row.
ordinal-numbers.short: Builds ordinal numbers from first to tenth.

days-and-months.full: Ordering the days of the week and the months of the year, and filling the gaps, builds the calendar sequence children use every morning.
days-and-months.short: Builds the sequence of days and months.

seasons.full: Sorting pictures into spring, summer, autumn and winter links weather, clothes and activities to the season they belong to.
seasons.short: Builds the four seasons and what belongs to each.

all-about-me.full: Drawing, counting and writing about themselves gives children a first page of their own to read, share and keep.
all-about-me.short: Builds self-description in words and pictures.

picture-word-cards.full: Cut-out cards with a clear picture and its word support matching, sorting and reading games at the table and on the wall.
picture-word-cards.short: Builds picture-word vocabulary with cut-out cards.

syllable-split.full: Marking the syllable breaks in longer words with arcs or bars shows children how a word is built and where to read it in parts.
syllable-split.short: Builds syllable division in longer words.

syllable-reading.full: Reading syllables and word families in rows, then writing the word, turns blending practice into whole words children can read.
syllable-reading.short: Builds blending from syllables and word families.

opposites.full: Matching each picture to its opposite builds pairs like big and small or hot and cold that anchor early vocabulary and comparison.

read-and-do.full: Reading a short instruction and doing exactly what it says makes every sentence a comprehension check the child can see on the page.
read-and-do.short: Builds reading comprehension by following directions.

rhyming-words.full: Finding the picture that rhymes and writing its word tunes the ear to word endings, the first step toward spelling patterns.
rhyming-words.short: Builds rhyme awareness and word endings.

hundreds-chart-puzzles.full: Filling the empty squares of a hundreds chart piece uses the row for tens and the column for ones, so every answer comes from position.
hundreds-chart-puzzles.short: Builds place value on the hundreds chart.

spelling-rules.full: Practising one spelling rule at a time across many words, then sorting words by the rule, makes the pattern stick beyond the word list.
spelling-rules.short: Builds spelling rules through sorting and writing.

compound-words.full: Joining two pictures into one compound word and splitting long words back into their parts shows how new words are built.
compound-words.short: Builds compound words from their parts.

verb-forms.full: Writing what someone does today and did yesterday beside each picture builds verb forms and tense in sentences children use.
verb-forms.short: Builds verb forms and simple tenses.

animal-fact-file.full: Completing a fact file about an animal, from its class and covering to what it eats, turns reading facts into organised writing.

logic-puzzles.full: Using clues to cross out and confirm cells in a logic grid trains step-by-step deduction until only one answer fits.
logic-puzzles.short: Builds logical deduction with grid puzzles.

division-with-remainder.full: Sharing a pile into equal groups and writing what is left over introduces remainders as the honest answer when division does not come out even.

feelings.full: Naming the feeling on each face and matching it to a situation gives children the words they need to say how they feel.
feelings.short: Builds feeling words and emotional awareness.

tangram.full: Cutting out the seven tans and fitting them into a shape trains children to see how big shapes are built from smaller ones and how a piece looks when it turns.
tangram.short: Builds shape composition with the seven tangram pieces.

human-body.full: Labelling the parts of a drawn child, counting how many of each we have and finding which come in twos gives children the names for their own body.
human-body.short: Builds the names of the parts of the body.

five-senses.full: Matching each object to the eye, ear, nose, tongue or hand that senses it, and sorting objects by sense, shows children how they explore the world.
five-senses.short: Builds the five senses and the organ for each.

weather-symbols.full: Reading the weather symbols on a chart, matching each to its word and keeping a weekly weather diary builds the words children use every morning.
weather-symbols.short: Builds weather symbols, words and a weekly chart.

recycling.full: Sorting empty packaging into the right bin by what it is made of teaches children the materials around them and why each has its own bin.
recycling.short: Builds sorting waste by material into the right bin.

cloze.full: Reading a whole sentence beside its picture and writing the one missing word trains children to use the picture and the sentence together to read.
cloze.short: Builds reading for meaning with a missing word.

odd-and-even.full: Pairing up the dots under a number and writing it as two equal parts shows children why a number is even or odd before they learn the last-digit rule.
odd-and-even.short: Builds odd and even numbers from pairs.

pronouns.full: Replacing a name with he, she or they under a portrait, and finding who a pronoun points back to, builds the small words that hold sentences together.

question-words.full: Reading an answer sentence and circling the question word that asks for the marked part trains children to see what who, what, where and when each ask for.
question-words.short: Builds question words from answer sentences.

rounding.full: Looking at the deciding digit and writing the nearest ten or hundred, then rounding first to estimate a sum, builds the rounding rule children use for checking.
rounding.short: Builds rounding to the nearest ten and hundred.

2d-shapes.full: Naming circles, squares, triangles and rectangles even when they are turned, stretched or small, and spotting the ones that only look close, builds true shape names.
2d-shapes.short: Builds naming flat shapes in any position.

road-safety.full: Reading which lamp is lit, following the steps to cross the road and learning what each road sign asks for gives children the rules that keep them safe outside.
road-safety.short: Builds traffic lights, crossing and road signs.

family.full: Finding each person on a family tree and naming them from one child's point of view builds the family words children use every day, from grandma to cousin.
family.short: Builds the family words and reading a family tree.

plants.full: Labelling the roots, stem, leaf, flower, fruit and seed of a whole plant, then asking what each part does and what a plant needs, builds a first plant science vocabulary.
plants.short: Builds the parts of a plant and what they do.

animal-life-cycles.full: Putting the egg, caterpillar, chrysalis and butterfly (and the frog's stages) in order around a circle shows children that animals change as they grow and start again.
animal-life-cycles.short: Builds the butterfly and frog life cycles in order.

earth-and-space.full: Deciding whether a fact is about the Sun, the Earth or the Moon, ordering the moon shapes and the planets, and explaining day and night builds a child's first picture of space.
earth-and-space.short: Builds the Sun, Earth, Moon, moon phases and planets.

maps.full: Reading a map key, seeing things from above, finding north, south, east and west and naming the continents and oceans builds the first map skills children need.
maps.short: Builds map keys, directions and continents.

digraphs.full: Saying each picture word and finding the two letters that make one sound, such as sh, ch and th, trains children to hear and read letter teams in new words.
digraphs.short: Builds hearing and reading letter teams.

synonyms.full: Finding the word that means the same, putting close words in order from a little to a lot and choosing a better word for said grows the vocabulary children write with.
synonyms.short: Builds words that mean the same and shades of meaning.

word-parts.full: Sorting words by their root word, finding the root that three words share and adding a prefix or a suffix shows children how words are built and what they mean.
word-parts.short: Builds root words, prefixes and suffixes.

story-sequencing.full: Numbering the pictures of a short story, choosing what happens next and retelling it with first, next, then and last builds the order and words children need to tell a story.
story-sequencing.short: Builds ordering a picture story and retelling it.

healthy-habits.full: Matching each habit to what we use, putting hand washing and tooth brushing in order and choosing the healthy way to cough gives children the daily habits that keep them well.
healthy-habits.short: Builds hand washing, tooth brushing and hygiene habits.

habitats.full: Matching animals to the ocean, forest, pond or polar ice, pairing them with their homes and seeing how their bodies suit a place builds a first picture of where animals live.
habitats.short: Builds animal habitats, homes and adaptations.

sink-or-float.full: Predicting whether each object will sink or float, testing it in water and recording what happened shows children that size alone does not decide, and starts real science thinking.
sink-or-float.short: Builds predicting, testing and recording sink or float.

cursive-writing.full: Tracing and writing joined letters in the school handwriting, practising the connections between letters and copying whole words builds a fluent, readable cursive hand.
cursive-writing.short: Builds joined cursive letters, words and sentences.
